title: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education - National Value Education - Pillars of Democracy
exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
subject: National Value Education

questions.q: In Civic Education, what is the meaning of the **"Pillars of Democracy"**?
options: The physical marble columns that support the National Assembly building in the capital
The fundamental principles, institutions, and values that uphold, support, and sustain a democratic system
The extremely wealthy politicians who fund all political parties
The heavy weapons used by the military to secure the nation's borders
questions.explain: Metaphorically, the **Pillars of Democracy** refer to the indispensable foundational institutions, principles (like the Rule of Law), and values that sustain the democratic process and keep society free.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Among the pillars of democracy, why are **"The People"** (the citizens) regarded as the most critical pillar?
options: Because they hold absolute sovereignty and have the ultimate power to elect or remove political leaders through voting
Because they secretly manufacture the electoral ballot boxes used in elections
Because they can aggressively dismantle democratic structures at will
Because they fund the national budget exclusively through bribery
questions.explain: In a democracy, sovereignty (ultimate authority) belongs entirely to **The People**. Without their active participation, consent, and votes, no democratic government can legitimately exist.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: The concept of **Majority Rule and Minority Rights** is a powerful pillar of democracy. What does this dual concept explicitly state?
options: The majority always wins elections and has the legal right to execute all minorities
Decisions are made based on what the majority of voters want, but the fundamental legal rights of the minority groups must always be protected and respected
The minority group is forced to surrender all their lands to the majority group after every election
Only minority tribes are allowed to form a democratic government
questions.explain: While democracy operates on **Majority Rule** (the candidate with the most votes wins), it strongly insists on protecting **Minority Rights** to ensure that smaller groups are not oppressed or marginalized by the majority.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Which of the following is absolutely required for an electoral process to be considered a strong **Pillar of Democracy**?
options: It must be heavily manipulated by the ruling party
It must be deeply opaque and hidden from the public
It must be highly transparent, free, fair, and unbiased
It must actively exclude voters aged 18 to 30
questions.explain: A **transparent electoral process** is a core pillar. Elections must be visibly free, fair, completely unbiased by INEC, and acceptable to the masses to confer true legitimacy on the winners.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: How does the **Rule of Law** act as a fundamental pillar that sustains democracy?
options: By ensuring the President can write any law independently of the National Assembly
By ensuring every citizen, including leaders, is equal before the law, thereby preventing dictatorial abuse of power
By allowing security forces to aggressively act without judicial warrants
By ensuring only the wealthy have strict access to legal defense
questions.explain: The **Rule of Law** supports democracy by firmly restricting arbitrary power. It guarantees that laws apply equally to the leaders and the led, thus preventing autocracy and safeguarding freedom.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Strong democratic institutions are considered pillars of democracy. Which of the following is a classic example of a strong democratic institution designed to curb government corruption?
options: A militant insurgent group
An independent, free press and active Civil Society Organizations (CSOs)
A secret state police operating without laws
An illegal smuggling syndicate
questions.explain: Institutions like a **free press**, CSOs, an independent judiciary, and anti-graft agencies function as powerful democratic pillars by ensuring transparency and holding the government accountable.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Identify the element below that is completely **destructive** to the pillars of democracy rather than supportive:
options: Active political opposition parties
Widespread political apathy among citizens
A totally independent judicial system
The separation of constitutional powers
questions.explain: **Political apathy** (when citizens completely lose interest in voting or political participation) actively destroys the pillar of 'The People', allowing bad leaders to hijack the system.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: The military taking over governance by violently overthrowing an elected democratic government fundamentally shatters which essential pillar?
options: Economic Inflation
Constitutional Supremacy and the Rule of Law
Traditional Monarchy
The Federal Character Principle
questions.explain: A military coup fundamentally violates **Constitutional Supremacy and the Rule of Law** because it uses armed force (arbitrary power) rather than electoral will to seize political control.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: In a democratic nation, if the Electoral Commission (INEC) is heavily controlled by the incumbent President, which pillar of democracy is immediately compromised?
options: Transparent Electoral Process
Absolute Monarchy
Minority Oppression
Freedom of Movement
questions.explain: If the electoral body is not totally independent, the **Transparent Electoral Process** is heavily compromised because the elections cannot be guaranteed to be free, fair, and unbiased.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Civic Education
questions.subject: National Value Education

questions.q: Why is a **"Transparent Electoral Process"** strongly regarded as an indispensable Pillar of Democracy?
options: It ensures that the incumbent President never loses an election
It completely hides the number of registered voters from the international community
It guarantees that the election results genuinely reflect the will of the people, granting true legitimacy to the newly elected leaders
It forces citizens to vote multiple times to boost the national turnout figures
questions.explain: Transparency ensures that elections are free, fair, and credible. When the process is **transparent**, citizens and the global community trust the results, which is what confers democratic **legitimacy** on the winners.
